sheet.base_note: Linear address in this dump. It moves with the EXE load segment. find_sheet_base() relocates it by matching terrain tile 0 and separator row 12.
sheet.rows_not_exported: y>=192 is the HIGH SCORE / menu / title bitmap and is not game art
sheet.index_atlas: gfx/anim/frames.u8 concatenates every frame in catalog order. atlas_offset is the byte start; 12x12 frames are 144 bytes and door frames are 576.

palette_cycle.direction: rotate right inside each group of four

not_found: No separate phaser or digging bitmap. Delete cycles the player through directional poses (right 10–15, left 34–39, up 52–57, down 58–60) and reads the map cell in front. Level 1 drew pose 10 exactly; the other poses and the tile-erase timing were not measured. TAS quotes 5, 26 and 56 frames for crate, light brick and dark brick; that clock was not re-measured.

Jet flame frames 4–9 and 28–33 are what EXE file 0xFEAA stores. Holding the jet key on level 6 produced the airborne poses 16, 17, 40 and 41 instead, so the flame cycle was not the bitmap at a sample.
Frame 61 and the pre-blit flash 65–70 are in the EXE and were not on screen.
Death group 72–77. The deaths captured held 83, 89 and 95.
Missile frames 22 and 27. The other ten missile frames were stored on level 5.
Flitzer frame 34. Frames 33 and 35–41 were stored on level 37.
Homer frame 20. Level 55 stayed on 19 for about 13 s. The EXE does define 20.
Spikes frames 17 and 18. Level 3 held 16. Batbot frames 43–46. Level 8 held 42.

Tubes, teleports, conveyors and toggles still have one bitmap each. Fuel and the gem are map tiles. Spark pixels are the palette cycle, not a second bitmap, and the breakup routine does not branch on spark versus enemy.

sprites.name: player_facing_a

states.name: walk_right
states.timing: (x >> 6) mod 4, from x before the step is added. One step per physics update, not a fixed IRQ period.

states.name: jet_right
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 7 while thrusting right. Two counter ticks per frame.

states.name: jet_idle_right
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 4 when the thrust axis is zero and the suit is still facing right.

states.name: phaser_right
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 10. Two counter ticks per frame. No separate beam bitmap; the routine then reads the map cell ahead.

states.name: phaser_right_alt
states.timing: Same cycle plus 3 when the alt byte is set.

states.name: airborne_right
states.timing: Single poses: 16 when horizontal speed is past 0x14, else 17. Level 6 stored both while the jet key was held.

sprites.note: Facing right, frame = column. Walk cols 0–3 are (x >> 6) mod 4, taken from x before the step is added (EXE file 0x10175). Levels 5 and 37 stored all four while x changed, and the bitmap of column 0 and column 1 was exact on level 1. There is no fixed IRQ period: the frame follows position. Cols 4–9 are the jet flame (EXE file 0xFEAA): (counter >> 1) mod 3, plus 7 when thrusting right, plus 4 when the thrust axis is zero, two counter ticks per step. Cols 10–12 are the phaser pose, not the jet (EXE file 0x1146B); level 1 drew column 10 exactly while Delete was held. Cols 16 and 17 are the airborne poses level 6 stored while the jet key was held. Cols 13–15 were not sampled, and the flame cycle in cols 4–9 did not run during that hold.

sprites.name: player_facing_b

states.name: jet_left
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 31.

states.name: jet_idle_left
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 28.

states.name: phaser_left
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 34, or +37 when the alt byte is set.

states.name: airborne_left
states.timing: 40 when horizontal speed is past 0x14, else 41. Level 6 stored both.

sprites.note: Facing left, frame = 24 + column. Walk frames 24–27 are the same (x >> 6) mod 4 plus 24 (EXE file 0x10175 when the facing word is negative). Levels 5 and 1 stored all four, and level 1 drew frames 24 and 26 with every opaque pixel matching the sheet. The left jet is frames 31–33 or 28–30 (EXE file 0xFED7 / 0xFEFF) and the left phaser is frames 34–39 (EXE file 0x113DA). Those were not sampled. Frames 40 and 41 (cols 16 and 17) are the left airborne poses and level 6 stored both while the jet key was held.

sprites.name: player_more

states.name: climb
states.timing: (y / 200) mod 4 + 48. Follows height, no fixed IRQ period.

states.name: phaser_up
states.timing: (counter >> 1) mod 3 + 52, plus 3 when the alt byte is set.

states.name: phaser_down
states.timing: (counter mod 3) + 58. One counter tick per frame.

states.name: airborne_state4
states.timing: Single pose when the state byte is 4.

states.name: flash
states.timing: Mostly 65/66 (counter bit 1) while counter mod 25 is 0..17; briefly 67/68 then 69/70.

states.name: breakup_hold_group0
states.timing: Hold when the death counter mod 100 has passed 35 and counter/100 is 0.

sprites.note: Climb is frames 48–51 (cols 0–3): (y / 200) mod 4 + 48 (EXE file 0x101AA). Level 1 drew all four, each an exact sheet match, while y changed on a ladder. The frame follows y, so it has no fixed IRQ period. Cols 4–13 are the up/down phaser poses (frames 52–60, EXE file 0x114B2 and 0x11513) and were not sampled. Cols 17–22 are frames 65–70, a counter flash written just before one blit (EXE file 0x142FA) and not seen. Col 23 is frame 71, the breakup hold for counter/100 = 0 (EXE file 0x1241A); the deaths captured were later groups and held 83, 89 and 95 instead.

sprites.name: player_breakup

states.name: breakup
states.timing: Six frames of 6 counter ticks, group = counter/100 (0..3), then hold 71, 83, 89 or 95. Captured holds were 83, 89 and 95. Each captured step lasted one 3-IRQ sample.

sprites.note: Death breakup, EXE file 0x123C2. While (counter mod 100) < 36 and counter < 1000, frame = (counter/100)*6 + ((counter mod 100)/6) mod 6 + 72. Each of those six steps is 6 counter ticks. After that the frame holds: 71 when counter/100 is 0, otherwise (counter/100)*6 + 77 (83, 89 or 95). Level 1 (died on a ladder) stored 84–89 and held 89; frames 86 and 89 matched the sheet exactly, and 84 was still the climb sprite, so the byte leads the blit by about one update. Level 8 stored 79–83 and held 83. Levels 6 and 37 stored 91–95 and held 95. Each of the six frames occupied one sample, and samples are 3 IRQ0 ticks apart, so the on-screen hold per frame is one sample under this DOSBox run. Group 72–77 did not come up. The same routine covers every death; nothing in it branches on enemy versus spark.

sprites.name: steel_ball

states.name: roll
states.timing: Two counter ticks per frame. Order 2,1,0 while the anim byte is below 64, else 0,1,2.

states.name: bounce
states.timing: Written for the bounce, not a timed cycle. Holds of 1–14 samples on level 1.

sprites.note: Roll, EXE file 0x15472. While the anim byte is below 0x40 the frame is 2 - ((byte >> 1) mod 3), so 2, 1, 0 for two counter ticks each. At or above 0x40 the frame is the remainder itself, 0, 1, 2. Frame 3 is written when the bounce flag is set (EXE file 0x154D0). Level 1 stored all four. Bounce holds were 1–14 samples and roll holds 1–4 samples; a sample is 3 IRQ0 ticks.

sprites.name: trackbot

states.name: walk_left
states.timing: Same plus 3 when velocity is negative.

sprites.note: Walk, EXE file 0x14E83: (x >> 6) mod 3 + 4, plus 3 when horizontal velocity is negative, so frames 4–6 and 7–9. Ladder, EXE file 0x14E58: (y >> 6) bit 0 + 10, frames 10–11. Level 37 stored all eight. While the bot was moving a frame usually lasted 1–2 samples (3–6 IRQ0 ticks); it also sat on one frame for the rest of a capture. The frame follows position, not a timer.

sprites.name: spring

states.name: turn_ground
states.timing: Set when the anim byte is 0 on a solid tile; the byte is then loaded with 10.

states.name: turn_ceiling
states.timing: Set when the anim byte is 1 on a solid tile; the byte is then loaded with 20.

sprites.note: Bob, EXE file 0x15924: (y / 200) bit 0 + 13, frames 13 and 14. Turn poses are immediates: frame 12 when the anim byte is 0 against a solid tile (the byte is then set to 10) and frame 15 when it is 1 (set to 20), EXE file 0x15905 and 0x15967. A level-16 capture stored all four. Bob holds were 1–8 samples and each turn pose was a single sample (3 IRQ0 ticks). How fast the anim byte counts is not separated from that. Level 55 left both springs on 13 for the whole 13 s, so the bob does not always run.

sprites.name: spikes

states.name: idle
states.timing: Init value. No per-frame cycle was found.

states.name: launch_pose
states.timing: (x >> 5) mod 3 + 16, in the block that also multiplies velocity by 20. Not shown to repeat.

sprites.note: Init frame is 16 (EXE file 0xDDBF and the same store at 0xE538). One later store, EXE file 0x16450, writes (x >> 5) mod 3 + 16, which can be 16, 17 or 18, but the same block multiplies both velocity words by 20, so it is a launch rather than a per-frame cycle. Level 3 held frame 16 on all four spikes for every sample. Frames 17 and 18 were not stored.

sprites.name: homer

states.name: blink_pose
states.timing: (counter >> 5) + 19, counter wraps at 64, so 32 counter ticks each. The 19 to 20 switch was not seen in 13 s.

sprites.note: EXE file 0x16D96 increments a byte, wraps it at 0x40, and stores (byte >> 5) + 19. That is frame 19 for 32 counter ticks, then frame 20 for 32, then repeat. Level 55 kept the byte at 19 for all 80 samples (about 13 s) while the playfield still changed by 5487 pixels, so the switch to frame 20 was not observed and the call rate of this routine is not known. Both columns use indices 247 and 254, so a homer on frame 19 still blinks with the palette cycle.

sprites.name: missile_up

states.name: up
states.timing: Facing 0 of (counter/10)*3 + ((counter>>1) mod 3) + 21. Two counter ticks per flame frame.

sprites.note: EXE file 0x15E32: frame = (counter / 10) * 3 + ((counter >> 1) mod 3) + 21. The /10 term is the facing (0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right) and the shift is the flame, two counter ticks per flame step. This row is facing 0, frames 21–23. Level 5 stored 21 and 23. Frame 22 was not in a sample. Holds of a single flame step were 1–4 samples (3–12 IRQ0 ticks).

sprites.name: missile_other

states.name: down
states.timing: Facing 1, same flame.

states.name: left
states.timing: Facing 2, same flame.

states.name: right
states.timing: Facing 3, same flame.

sprites.note: Facings 1–3 of the same formula: frames 24–26, 27–29 and 30–32. Level 5 stored 24, 25, 26, 28, 29, 30, 31 and 32. Frame 27 (column 3) was not in a sample. Frame 32 matched the sheet at one cell with every opaque pixel. Flame holds were 1–4 samples, the same as the upward facing.

sprites.name: flitzer

states.name: direction
states.timing: (counter / 20) + 33. Capture stored 33 and 35–41, jumping rather than counting, usually for 1–3 samples.

sprites.note: EXE file 0x16B22 stores (counter / 20) + 33. Frame 33 is the value it has at rest. Level 37 stored 33 and 35–41. Frame 34 was not in a sample. The byte jumps (33 then 38 then 37) instead of counting up, and a frame then sat for 58 samples, so this is a direction id rather than a 9-step cycle. When it did change, the new frame usually lasted 1–3 samples (3–9 IRQ0 ticks).

sprites.name: batbot

states.name: rise
states.timing: While vertical velocity is positive. Level 8 stayed on 42 for every sample.

states.name: fly
states.timing: (counter >> 4) / 3 + 42. Three high-nibble steps share a frame. Frames 43–46 were not stored.

sprites.note: EXE file 0x17374 writes frame 42 while vertical velocity is positive. Otherwise frame = (counter >> 4) / 3 + 42, and another block adds 0x10 to that counter while a timer is below 15, then clears the high nibble. Quotients 0–4 are frames 42–46; three increments of the high nibble share one frame. Col 23 duplicates an earlier cell and is not its own frame number. Level 8 held frame 42 for every sample. Frames 43–46 were not stored.

sprites.name: door
sprites.note: Eight unique 24×24 opaque frames. Level 16, with one gem placed on the player's right and the enemies removed, drew frame 0 closed, then frames 1 through 7 in order. Each of 1–6 was on screen for one sample and frame 7 then held. Samples are 3 IRQ0 ticks apart and no opening frame was skipped or repeated, so the door advances one frame per 3 IRQ0 ticks and stays on the open frame. The 38-frame delay after the last gem (TAS) falls inside the sample before frame 1 and was not measured on its own.
